Promoting British Values
The DfE have reinforced the need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
Schools, through their curriculum, are legally bound to actively promote fundamental British values.
How does Ripple Primary School ‘actively promote…’ British values:
Democracy – what do we do?
Rule of law – what do we do?
Individual liberty – what do we do?
Respect and tolerance – what do we do?

Welcome
On behalf of all the staff, children, parents and governors I would like to welcome you to Ripple Primary School, an EMOTIONALLY AVAILABLE SCHOOL where EVERYONE IS WELCOME and EVERYONE BELONGS.
BELONGING is the most powerful word we can use in making our Ripple family a genuinely INCLUSIVE school community where NURTURE is at the heart of everything we do.
NURTURE in schools is about providing an environment where all children and young people (and the grownups) feel that they BELONG. A genuine feeling of BELONGING is fundamental to forming strong, positive relationships (child-child, child-adult, adult-adult). Strong, positive relationships are the foundation on which social, emotional and mental wellbeing are based and they underpin the development of resilience and security.
Children and young people who truly feel that they BELONG in their school will be better attenders, better behaved, better engaged and will consequently better achieve and attain; academically, socially and emotionally.
Ripple is a very happy and welcoming school with a community focussed outlook and we are committed to the safety and care of all our pupils and their families.
As one of the largest primary schools in the UK, with a school population of nearly 900 across two sites, we are able to provide an exciting range of learning opportunities for our children and a very high level of support for our families.
Our aim is to provide the highest quality education for all in a caring, supportive, nurturing and inclusive learning environment. We offer a stimulating curriculum where teachers and children work together to ensure that high quality teaching and learning opportunities are always at the heart of everything we do. We also offer a wide range of enrichment activities that are intended to be both inspirational and aspirational for all of our children.
We are very proud to be part of the UNICEF Rights Respecting Schools Award programme, which ensures that the voice of our pupils is always heard.
We are proud of the school’s many achievements, which have been the result of our successful and hard working partnership between our staff, our children and our families.
We hope that you enjoy browsing our school website and that it gives you an insight into all that we do at Ripple. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any comments, suggestions or if we can help you in any other way.
Roger Mitchell Headteacher

PSHE/RSE
Our intentions at Ripple are to teach children life skills of the PSHE and RSE curriculum. In line with the National Curriculum 2014, all schools must provide a curriculum that is broadly based, balanced and meets the needs of all pupils. Under section 78 of the Education Act 2002 and the Academies Act 2010, a PSHE curriculum: ● Promotes the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical development of pupils at the school and of society, and ● Prepares pupils at the school for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of later life. Through quality delivery, our PSHE programme aims to develop: ● confident individuals who know and understand how to live safe, happy, healthy, fulfilling lives; ● young people who are able to maintain positive, respectful and healthy relationships, within which they can thrive personally and socially; ● responsible citizens who understand they have rights and responsibilities that help them make a positive contribution to society; and ● successful learners who enjoy overall learning, making progress and achieving success

Curriculum Lead & Assistant Headteacher: Mrs Liaw
Wider Curriculum
Stephanie Liaw
As the Curriculum Lead at Ripple Primary School, I am deeply passionate about empowering and inspiring children to reach their full potential. I am committed to being a part of developing and providing a rich and diverse curriculum that ensures every child has ample opportunities to build cultural capital, broadening their horizons and fostering a love for learning. My goal is to ensure that all children make rapid progress over time, equipping them with the skills and knowledge they need to succeed. At Ripple we are dedicated to nurturing a love of school, helping our students grow into lifelong learners who are curious, confident, and ready to thrive in the future.
As part of my role, I collaborate closely with staff, outside agencies, different schools, and various departments to develop a cohesive and dynamic curriculum tailored to our students' needs. Currently, I am finishing a Curriculum for Senior Leaders Course, which has provided me with up-to-date professional development to advance our curriculum using the latest research and practices. As a result of my professional development, I prioritise sharing this knowledge with subject leaders so we can foster a culture of continuous improvement.

MFL: French
At Ripple the French curriculum provides our students with a comprehensive and immersive learning experience that equips pupils with the skills and knowledge needed to become confident and proficient French speakers. By integrating various teaching methods and resources we aim to create a dynamic and engaging learning environment that motivates our students to excel in their language studies. Our ultimate goal is to prepare our students for real-world communication and cultural understanding in the French speaking world.
At Ripple, our goal is to embrace and celebrate our achievements, differences and the cultural diversity within our school community. By offering foreign language instruction, we aim to highlight the value of linguistic diversity and promote a deeper understanding of other cultures.
To ensure that all teachers feel confident in teaching French we have implemented Kapow Primary’s French scheme of work. This comprehensive program is designated to foster a love for language learning and cultivate an appreciation for different cultures, aligning with our school’s mission statement.
Our objective is to empower students to effectively communicate in French for practical purposes, both orally and in writing. By building a strong foundation in language learning, we hope to inspire students to explore additional languages, enhance their understanding of the English language, and create opportunities for further study and career prospects in an international setting.
Kapow Primary’s French curriculum is structured to support students in meeting the national curriculum standards for KS2. While KS1 does not have specific language attainment targets, our EYFS and KS1 classes are exposed to French through songs, basic greetings and visual displays.
Additionally, we have dedicated subject specialist teachers for Lower Key Stage 2 and Upper Key Stage 2 French lessons. All classroom teachers are equipped to teach these lessons effectively by utilising the detailed lesson plans and instructional videos provided by Kapow. Through this approach, we strive to ensure that all students receive a comprehensive and engaging French language education at Ripple.
